How do I get around the paywall on news sites like the NYT or WSJ?

Here are several practical methods people use to get around paywalls on news sites like the NYT or WSJ. The NYT has a metered paywall (easier to bypass), while WSJ has a harder paywall, but the methods below cover both.

### 1. Archive snapshots (most reliable for WSJ & NYT)
- **archive.today / archive.ph**  
  Go to `https://archive.today/` or `https://archive.ph/`, paste the article URL into the top box, and press Enter. If a snapshot already exists, it loads immediately; otherwise it will create one.
- **Wayback Machine**  
  Go to `https://web.archive.org/` and paste the URL. Look for a recent snapshot.

### 2. Browser extensions
- **Bypass Paywalls Clean**  
  This is a well-known open-source extension for Firefox, Chrome, and Edge. It automatically removes paywalls on hundreds of sites, including NYT and WSJ.  
  - Firefox: available directly from the Firefox Add-ons site.  
  - Chrome/Edge: install from GitHub (the extension is not in the Chrome Web Store).  
  It updates frequently and works with many hard paywalls.
- **uBlock Origin / NoScript**  
  Blocking JavaScript can sometimes prevent the paywall overlay from loading. This works better on some sites than others.

### 3. Incognito/private window + clearing cookies (for NYT metered paywall)
- Open the article in a private/incognito window.  
- When you hit the NYT’s monthly free article limit, clear cookies for `nytimes.com` or use a different browser profile, then continue reading.  
- You can also use a cookie manager extension to delete only NYT cookies quickly.

### 4. Reader mode / text extraction
- In Firefox, Safari, or Edge, click the **reader view** icon in the address bar as the page is loading. Sometimes this shows the full article text before the paywall activates.  
- Use text-extraction sites like:  
  - `https://www.textise.net/`  
  - `https://www.printfriendly.com/`  
  Paste the URL, and the service extracts the article text.

### 5. Change your user agent to Googlebot
Many news sites serve full content to search engine crawlers so their articles appear in Google results. You can set your browser’s user agent to Googlebot to get the same treatment.

**How to do it in Chrome/Edge/Firefox:**
1. Open Developer Tools (F12).
2. Go to the **Network conditions** tab (Chrome/Edge) or the **Responsive Design Mode** (Firefox).
3. Uncheck “Use browser default” and paste a Googlebot user agent string, for example:
   ```
   Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1; +http://www.google.com/bot.html)
   ```
4. Refresh the article page.

### 6. Referer trick
Some sites allow access if the referring page is Google, Facebook, or Twitter. You can use a redirect link:
- Google: `https://www.google.com/url?q=<full-article-url>`
- Facebook: `https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=<full-article-url>`

Clicking through these sometimes grants access because the site thinks you came from a social/search referrer.

### 7. Disable JavaScript for the site
- Use an extension like uBlock Origin or NoScript to block JavaScript on the news site.
- Reload the article. If the paywall is implemented in JavaScript, the full text may appear.
- In some browsers you can also temporarily disable JavaScript in settings.

### 8. Text-only/cached versions
- Search the article headline on Google or Bing. Next to the result, look for a **cached** or **text-only** version.  
- Google has removed most cache links, but Bing still offers cached pages sometimes.  
- You can also try searching the exact headline in quotes on Google, then open the result using the referer trick above.

### 9. Library access (free and legitimate)
Many public libraries offer free digital access to NYT, WSJ, and other paywalled publications:
- Check your library’s website for “PressReader,” “ProQuest,” or “New York Times Digital” access.  
- Some libraries provide 24-hour or 7-day passes you can redeem from home with your library card.
- The NYT also offers free access through many university libraries.

### 10. Apple News / Google News
- Apple News+ and Google News sometimes show full articles or extended previews from paywalled sources.  
- Searching the headline in Apple News or Google News may give you a readable version.

For **WSJ specifically**, the most reliable free methods tend to be `archive.today`, the Bypass Paywalls Clean extension, or the Googlebot user agent switch. For **NYT**, incognito + clearing cookies or a metered-paywall reset often works, and the archive sites are also effective.
